source.title_on_document: Artificial Creativity? Evaluating AI Against Human Performance in Creative Interpretation of Visual Stimuli

supplement.holds: No supplementary document is cited and no appendix appears in the complete article (PDF pp. 1-13).

paper_design_summary: ChatGPT-4 and human participants gave creative interpretations of a set of ambiguous, abstract figures (the Figural Interpretation Quest). The study measured the flexibility of the interpretations and collected subjective creativity ratings from independent evaluators. No participant used AI; AI output is compared with human output.

studies.label: ChatGPT-4 versus humans on the Figural Interpretation Quest

assignment.prereg_locator: https://osf.io/xv3n2/?view_only=1d9a96705c3c4b79aa9207ba52295ee9 (PDF p. 4, article p. 3, section 2 Method: hypotheses and data-analysis process; deviations described in the article, including added raters in section 2.3, PDF p. 6, article p. 5).

participants.exclusions: 310 individuals accessed the study link; 279 completed the study; 256 passed attention checks. Excluding participants with an empty response or a response longer than three words left 247 valid human participants. One further participant was excluded because SemDis could not calculate a flexibility score, leaving 246 analyzed for both outcomes (Table 1).
participants.who: Native English speakers recruited through Prolific. The 246 analyzed human participants are distinct from 247 ChatGPT-4 test sessions and 11 psychology-student raters; AI sessions and raters are not counted as creative-task participants.
participants.country: UK (166), USA (79), Canada (9), and Ireland (2), reported for the 256 participants who passed attention checks; final-sample country counts are not stated.
participants.quote: Data from the remaining 246 participants were analyzed according to the pre-registered data analysis protocol.
participants.locator: PDF p. 5 (article p. 4), section 2.1 Participants; PDF p. 6 (article p. 5), section 2.3 Scoring; PDF p. 7 (article p. 6), Results and Table 1, note a

ai_tool.how_used: ChatGPT-4 produced its own interpretations of the figures; no human used AI.

task.description: Figural Interpretation Quest (FIQ): give two creative interpretations of each of four ambiguous, abstract figures, aiming to make the two interpretations as semantically different as possible. The same figures appeared in the same fixed order for humans and ChatGPT-4. Humans received a practice image and an explanation of semantic distance; ChatGPT-4 received the same test images and task instructions without the practice image. AI response limits of 1, 2, or 3 words, excluding common English stop words, were chosen to match the human response-length distribution (PDF pp. 5-6, article pp. 4-5, sections 2.1-2.2).
task.duration: Humans: 30 seconds per figure to enter two interpretations (PDF p. 5, article p. 4, section 2.2); no corresponding AI time limit is stated.

outcomes.name: Subjectively perceived creativity of interpretations
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Eleven psychology students from the University of Bergen or University of Turku rated each interpretation on a 0-2 creativity scale, blind to whether it came from humans or AI. The initial three raters were supplemented by eight because reliability was weak; interpretation order was randomized separately for each rater. Mixed models analyze single interpretations, with random intercepts for human participants or AI sessions; Table 1 summarizes scores averaged across each participant/session's responses to the four figures. Figure-specific models are variants of the same outcome. The total number of analyzed interpretations is not explicitly reported (PDF p. 6, article p. 5, sections 2.3-2.4; PDF pp. 7-8, article pp. 6-7, Table 1 and Creativity).

contrasts.reported: Table 1, averages across each participant/session's responses: GPT-4 N = 247 test sessions, mean = 0.632, SD = 0.0795, 95% CI [0.622, 0.642]; humans N = 246 people, mean = 0.738, SD = 0.0827, 95% CI [0.728, 0.749]. Overall mixed-model contrast (human minus GPT-4): B = 0.107, SE = 0.008, 95% CI [0.090, 0.124], t(1946) = 12.64, p < .001. Three humans (1.2%) had a total creativity score, defined as the mean across interpretations to the four figures, above the best GPT-4 session's total score.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 7 (article p. 6), Table 1, section 3.1 Descriptive statistics and correlations, and Overall performance

outcomes.name: Flexibility of interpretations
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: SemDis semantic distance between the two interpretations of the same figure by a human participant or AI session, averaged across five semantic spaces. The multiplicative compositional model and remove-filler-and-clean preprocessing were used. This measures flexibility within a participant/session's response pair, not diversity across people. Mixed models analyze single semantic-distance scores with random intercepts for human participants or AI sessions; Table 1 summarizes scores averaged across the four figures. Figure-specific models are variants of this outcome. The total number of analyzed pairs is not explicitly reported (PDF p. 6, article p. 5, sections 2.3-2.4; PDF pp. 7-8, article pp. 6-7, Table 1 and Flexibility).

contrasts.reported: Table 1, averages across each participant/session's responses: GPT-4 N = 247 test sessions, mean = 0.934, SD = 0.0231, 95% CI [0.931, 0.937]; humans N = 246 people, mean = 0.899, SD = 0.0626, 95% CI [0.891, 0.906]. Overall mixed-model contrast (human minus GPT-4): B = −0.036, SE = 0.004, 95% CI [-0.044, −0.027], t(484.04) = −8.493, p < .001. Thirteen humans (5.3%) exceeded the best GPT-4 session in total flexibility. The mean comparison favors AI, whereas the highest observed human score exceeds the highest AI score; these are different summaries.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 7 (article p. 6), Table 1, section 3.1 Descriptive statistics and correlations, and Overall performance

outcomes.name: Unique responses across each group's output pool
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Descriptive count of distinct responses in each group's complete response pool: humans produced 794 unique responses, versus 385 responses for ChatGPT-4, described as a smaller range for AI. This differs from semantic distance within a participant/session's two interpretations. A detailed deduplication procedure and inferential uncertainty are not reported (PDF p. 7, article p. 6, section 3.1; PDF pp. 9-10, article pp. 8-9, Discussion).

contrasts.reported: Humans produced 794 unique responses; ChatGPT-4 produced 385 responses, described as a smaller overall range of responses for AI. These are response counts, not people, raters, or test sessions. Only descriptive counts are reported; no standard error, interval, or statistical test is given for this comparison.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 7 (article p. 6), section 3.1 Descriptive statistics and correlations; PDF pp. 9-10 (article pp. 8-9), Discussion

diversity_detail.metric: Number of unique responses in each group's pool
diversity_detail.computed_over: The full pool of responses across human participants, compared with the full pool across separate ChatGPT-4 sessions.
diversity_detail.uncertainty: No standard error, confidence interval, or statistical test is reported for these counts.
diversity_detail.notes: A detailed deduplication procedure is not reported. This is an AI-versus-human output comparison, not an effect of AI assistance on human diversity.

sample_overlap.shares_participants_with: Human data were collected as part of another study, previously preregistered at https://osf.io/fy3mn/?view_only=f1cf960d0170433dba9d31df68a6eaf7. The article does not identify another publication or atlas cid for that sample.
sample_overlap.quote: Human participant data were collected as part of another study, and such data collection was previously pre-registered at OSF.io
sample_overlap.locator: PDF p. 6 (article p. 5), end of section 2.2

eligibility.reason: The study analyzed 246 human participants, meeting the people-count criterion (PDF p. 7, article p. 6, Results and Table 1). Humans and ChatGPT-4 independently interpreted the figures; no people were assigned to AI assistance, so criterion 1 is not met and core remains no (PDF pp. 5-6, article pp. 4-5, sections 2.1-2.2). Human creativity ratings and automated flexibility scores assess produced interpretations, meeting criterion 3 (PDF p. 6, article p. 5, sections 2.3-2.4). This is ai_vs_human context evidence.

one_line_finding: Among 246 humans and 247 ChatGPT-4 sessions, humans had higher mean rated creativity (0.738 vs 0.632), whereas ChatGPT-4 had higher mean flexibility (0.934 vs 0.899), and the highest human scores exceeded the highest AI scores on both measures (PDF p. 7, article p. 6, Table 1 and section 3.1).
